targets.authors: Fergus, T. A., Bardeen, J. R., & Wu, K. D.
targets.title: Intolerance of uncertainty and uncertainty-related attentional biases: Evidence of facilitated engagement or disengagement difficulty?
targets.evidence_quote: This report aimed to conceptually replicate the results of Fergus et al. (Cognitive Therapy and Research 37:735-741, 2013).
targets.outcome_quote: We partially replicated the results of Fergus et al. (Cognitive Therapy and Research 37:735-741, 2013). We found that higher IU was significantly associated with faster identification of uncertainty-based information, relative to neutral information. However, we also observed a similar pattern of results for trait anxiety. Additionally, we observed no specificity of IU or trait anxiety in predicting faster identification of uncertainty-based information, relative to neutral information.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly judge the replication partial: the IU association replicated but its specificity did not.
